About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp's Enterprise Customer Success Managers on the Lifecycle team don't stop at go-live — they make sure customers keep getting more from Ramp as their business grows. Ramp has grown its product suite significantly over the last several years. As we've matured as an organization, our customer relationships have grown more complex too: customers are buying more of the platform at once, running it across more entities and teams, and relying on it for more of how their finance function operates. Hitting an activation milestone doesn't mean the job's finished. Too often, a feature that could solve a real problem goes unused because no one is there to show how it would work in that customer's business.

That's where you come in. This is a role for people who understand how finance teams actually run, who think in years rather than quarters, and who already use AI the way surgeons use instruments: not occasionally, not as an experiment, but as the default way they work. You'll own the customer experience after implementation for a book of Ramp's highest-potential enterprise customers, partnering with Account Management on long-term account strategy. You'll also be one of the first Lifecycle CSMs on a newly formed team, helping define how Ramp earns and keeps the trust of its most important customers.

What You'll Do

  • Own the post-implementation experience for a book of enterprise customers, with clear accountability for sustained adoption, customer satisfaction, and renewal readiness

  • Drive sustained adoption by understanding each customer's goals and guiding them toward the workflows that improve outcomes for their business — including the products and features they've already purchased but haven't fully put to work

  • Act as each customer's expert in finance workflows: understand how they run their business, advise on decisions as their needs change, and make the value of new Ramp capabilities clear in their context

  • Build multi-threaded relationships across every account and partner with Account Management on executive relationships, so the account stays steady through change like a new Controller or CFO

  • Partner with Account Management on QBRs and executive business reviews, quantifying Ramp's impact in the language CFOs and Controllers care about — close cycle improvement, spend visibility, savings, and ROI — not just product usage metrics

  • Spot opportunities for growth and bring them to Account Management, who owns renewals and expansion; as customers add products, drive ongoing activation so they reach value quickly

  • Run your book on data: monitor usage, CP, and risk signals, get ahead of challenges and escalations, and see them through to resolution well before renewal is on the calendar

  • Use AI tools daily to prepare for customer calls, build materials, synthesize data, identify account risk, and operate at a pace traditional methods can't match

  • Bring customer feedback back into Ramp — surfacing patterns, gaps, and opportunities from your accounts to shape how Ramp evolves

  • Help build the motion from the ground up: executive sponsor programs, champion groups, churn reviews, and the playbooks every future Lifecycle CSM will run

Must-Haves

  • Long-term account ownership — You've owned a book of customers past launch and through renewal, and you have measurable retention, adoption, or satisfaction results to show for it. Finance or fintech context is a plus but not required.

  • Customer experience mindset — You measure success by how customers feel about working with you, not only by milestones hit. You get ahead of problems before customers raise them and own escalations through resolution.

  • Executive relationship building — You build multi-threaded relationships across finance, operations, and the C-suite. When your champion leaves, the account doesn't leave with them.

  • Financial impact communication — You can walk a CFO through the value Ramp has delivered, connect adoption to P&L outcomes, and help make the case for continued investment in financial terms, not product terms. A finance background is not required — fluency is.

  • AI fluency as a daily habit — You already use AI tools habitually in your work. You use them to prep for calls, synthesize information, build customer-facing materials, and automate repetitive tasks. This is how you work, not something you're exploring. Ramp is a builder culture: if you don't instinctively reach for AI before doing things manually, this role will be a hard adjustment.

  • Data-driven book management — You prioritize your time based on usage, revenue, and risk signals, not on who emailed last. You can spot an at-risk account months before renewal and know what to do about it.

  • Technical and systems acumen — You're comfortable around major ERP platforms (NetSuite, SAP S/4HANA, Workday, Sage Intacct, or similar) and understand how Ramp fits into a customer's finance stack. You don't need to code, but you can diagnose what's blocking adoption and bring in the right technical partner.

  • Builder mindset — You're energized by building something that doesn't exist yet. This team is new, and you'll help shape the playbooks, programs, and rituals that define how Lifecycle CSMs work, all while running your own book. You bring structure to ambiguity and iterate quickly when something isn't working.

  • 7+ years in enterprise customer success, account management, or consulting — You've spent enough time with complex organizations and senior stakeholders that it's second nature. You know how to keep an enterprise customer successful long after the launch.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Consumption-based revenue experience — You've worked with a product where value is measured in usage or spend, not seats, and know how to grow adoption after the contract is signed.

  • Finance domain depth — Exposure to FP&A, accounting software ecosystems (NetSuite, Sage, QuickBooks, Xero), expense management, or CFO-adjacent workflows. Accelerates credibility with Ramp's customer base.

  • Demonstrated commercial impact — You can point to retention, adoption, or renewal outcomes with specific metrics attached — not described in general terms.

About Morpho

Morpho is a leading Decentralized Finance (DeFi) lending protocol backed by a16z crypto, Paradigm, Ribbit Capital, Apollo, Vaneck, Coinbase Ventures, Variant and 50 others to build an open credit network giving anyone, anywhere, access to the best possible terms. Morpho is experiencing exponential adoption, with over billion in deposits on the network and used by institutional clients including Bitwise, Galaxy, and Anchorage Digital and the largest crypto exchanges, such as Coinbase, Binance, and Kraken. Now, Morpho is scaling its team of contributors to establish itself as the open credit network, not just of DeFi, but of the world.

 

Why Morpho Exists

Everyone has the potential to build something great for the world. But fulfilling that ambition almost always requires more: people willing to trust you with their capital. Yet access to capital still depends on where you live, who you know, and which institutions are willing to trust you. Even when capital is available, it sits fragmented across disconnected networks and hidden behind intermediaries. The result is a system that fails most of the people it should serve. Borrowers overpay. Lenders earn less than they should. Many are shut out entirely, not because they are unworthy of credit, but because today's infrastructure was never built to connect them. Morpho exists to solve this. Full article here.

Location

New York preferred. Remote is possible between GMT-5 and GMT+2.

 

Role

Banks, asset managers and token issuers are bringing stocks, funds and other real-world assets onchain. Those assets become far more useful once their holders can borrow against them and lend them out. Midnight, Morpho's fixed-rate, fixed-term lending protocol, gives institutions the predictable terms they need to do that.

 

This role owns the products that make Morpho the credit layer for institutional assets, spanning tokenized equities and funds as collateral, loans backed by assets held with a qualified custodian, and the onchain equivalents of repo and securities lending.

 

Close partnership with institutions is central to this role. You will develop a detailed understanding of how they operate across trading, custody and compliance, and translate their requirements into products that scale across many partners.

 

Responsibilities

 

  • Own the vision, strategy and roadmap for institutional credit on Morpho, end to end.

  • Act as Morpho's domain expert on the institutional market. Go deep with issuers, asset managers, banks, custodians and brokers on how they finance and lend assets, represent Morpho with them, and turn conflicting input into precise problem statements and requirements.

  • Decide which issuers and asset types come first, which wait and which Morpho declines, and make the trade-offs explicit.

  • Judge which partner-specific requests become standard capabilities many institutions can use, and make the build or partner call for each.

  • Work as a peer to the protocol team on design trade-offs, bringing legal and risk in early on custody, transfer restrictions, valuation and liquidation for each asset type.

  • Drive each initiative from problem definition through launch and adoption, across teams you do not manage. Define success before launch, measured in active loans.

 

What Success Looks Like

 

First 30 days

You understand Morpho's lending stack and what Midnight makes possible. You have met protocol, markets, vaults, solutions, business development and legal, and joined live conversations with issuers and asset managers. You have written down where the issuer product stands and what blocks its first launch.

 

First 3 months

The first issuers are onboarding to a defined product with standard terms. You have a ranked view of the next two institutional loan types, backed by partner evidence, with named partners in conversation for each.

 

First 6 months

Issuers are live and holders of their assets are borrowing. A second institutional loan type has a working proof of concept with real counterparties. New institutions onboard through a repeatable process, not a custom project.

 

Must Have Experience & Skills

  • Shipped products for institutional users in capital markets or securities finance: repo, securities lending, prime brokerage, collateral management, custody or tokenized assets.

  • A track record of taking a product from zero to one, where you found the opportunity and carried it through launch.

  • Working knowledge of how institutions hold, finance and lend assets, and of the regulatory and operational constraints that shape those products.

  • Comfortable leading conversations with senior people at banks, asset managers and issuers, and turning them into clear requirements.

  • Able to deliver through influence across teams, without a dedicated engineering team.

  • Clear writing and speaking for technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Creates clarity and drives decisions in ambiguous situations, and acts without waiting to be told.

  • Team-first mindset, low ego.

 

Nice to Have

  • Experience with onchain lending, tokenization or digital asset custody.

  • Time on both sides: at a traditional financial institution and at a technology company.

  • Has been a founder, or owned a new product line end to end.

Perks & Benefits

We design benefits around deep work and growth, so you can do the best work of your career. Expect fair, top-tier compensation, real flexibility, time together in Paris, great health coverage, and support to keep learning.

 

Equal Opportunity

We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and hire based on talent, potential, and values alignment.

If you have spent your career in SOX, internal controls, audit, controllership, or financial close, and you want to build the systems that fix what you find instead of only testing them, this role is for you.

Why this role exists 

Every product BitGo ships eventually becomes a number: a balance, a fee, a statement, a journal entry, a regulatory filing. As a public company and a federally chartered trust bank, we have to prove those numbers are right every period, across many products, legal entities, and jurisdictions. 

You will own the product strategy for the financial and accounting platform that makes those numbers right by construction, as we add products, entities, and asset types. You will turn accounting requirements into scalable, auditable, self-service platform capabilities that product, engineering, finance, and compliance can build on. 

Digital assets make this harder, and more interesting, than it is at a traditional bank. On chain activity, custody structures, staking, tokenized assets, and settlement each move through our systems differently, and each has to land correctly on the books. The industry is still writing the playbook for much of this. You will help write it. 

Level 

We are hiring at Senior or Principal level, depending on experience. The core scope is the same at both. At Principal, you have already set platform strategy, led accounting systems, or established control standards that multiple teams adopted, and you will own the crossproduct standards and the working relationship with finance and audit leadership with more independence from day one.

Two paths to this role 

There is more than one way to be great at this job. You may come from product management and built financial compliance platforms. You may come from audit, controllership, or accounting systems and have spent years finding where numbers break, and then built the thing that fixed it. We are just as interested in the second group. If you are an auditor or accountant with a builder mindset, you will be evaluated on the same scope and the same bar as a product manager. What matters is that you have shipped: tools, automation, control frameworks, or systems that other teams adopted and kept using.

What you will own 

  • The financial data and accounting platform roadmap: Define and deliver the shared capabilities that make financial data trustworthy by construction: ledger and sub-ledger integrity, balance and activity reconciliation, fee and revenue calculation, client reporting, and the feeds into the general ledger and the financial close. 
  • Controls built into the product: Partner with finance, internal audit, and external auditors to turn SOX and internal control requirements into product capabilities instead of manual procedures. When a control needs a build, you own the requirements, the plan, and the timeline, delivered in step with the audit calendar. 
  • Platform standards across products and entities: Make sure new products, new asset types, new legal entities, and acquisitions plug into the platform instead of creating bespoke accounting workarounds. You set the standards, interfaces, and data contracts that product teams build against. 
  • Regulatory and audit readiness: Work with compliance, legal, and risk so the platform supports regulatory reporting, books-and-records requirements, and examiner and auditor requests. You run dated plans against external deadlines and flag early when a timeline is at risk. 
  • Close, reporting, and operational efficiency: Reduce the manual effort, elapsed time, and risk in month-end and quarter-end close. Establish the metrics that show whether the platform is working: reconciliation breaks, close duration, audit adjustments, manual journal volume, and time to onboard a new product. 

What success looks like in the first two quarters 

  • A documented map of how each major product's financial activity reaches the general ledger, with manual steps and gaps identified and prioritized. 
  • A dated platform roadmap agreed with finance, engineering, and compliance, with external deadlines (audit, regulatory, and reporting) built into the plan. 
  • One high-impact capability shipped end to end, such as automated reconciliation for a key product, that measurably reduces manual work or control risk. 

Who you will partner with 

  • Finance and Accounting leadership own accounting policy and judgment. You translate their requirements into platform capabilities and make the product the system of record. 
  • Engineering leadership owns architecture, estimates, and delivery. You partner on sequencing, platform design, and tradeoffs without positional authority. Product Managers across Custody, Trading, Staking, and Financing need the platform to support their products without becoming a bottleneck. 
  • Compliance, Legal, and Risk own regulatory judgment. You build the delivery process behind it. 
  • Internal and external audit rely on you to plan control-related work clearly and deliver it on schedule. 
  • Commercial and client teams need accurate statements, reporting, and billing that clients can trust. 

What we're looking for 

  • 6+ years of experience (typically 9+ for Principal) building or scaling systems, platforms, tooling, or control frameworks that multiple internal or external teams relied on, including 3+ years as the owner. You might have done this as a product manager, or from audit, controllership, or accounting systems. At Principal, you have set strategy or standards that other teams adopted.
  • An accounting or finance foundation: a CPA or equivalent, an accounting degree, or hands-on experience in financial reporting, audit, controllership, or accounting systems. You can read a trial balance, follow a journal entry through a ledger, and discuss revenue recognition or reconciliation with a controller without a translator.
  • Experience building scalable platforms such as ledgers, billing, payments, reporting, data infrastructure, reconciliation tooling, or controls automation. You think in data models, interfaces, and reuse, and you know when a one-off fix will cost us later. If you come from audit or accounting, this may look like automating reconciliations, building controls into a system, or designing data models and tooling with engineers, rather than a formal product title.
  • Experience in a regulated financial environment. You have worked with auditors, examiners, SOX controls, or control programs, and you understand how public company obligations change how products are built and shipped.
  • Technical credibility with Engineers. You can follow an architecture discussion, pressure-test an estimate, and write precise requirements for data-heavy systems. Familiarity with SQL and financial data pipelines is a plus.
  • Crypto or digital-asset experience is a requirement. If you do not have professional experience, passion projects with breadth and depth across digital assets could be a good fit.
  • A writing-first approach: your default artifacts are clear specs, data flow maps, and decision documents.

What will make you fail here 

  • Building bespoke solutions for each product or blockchain instead of platform capabilities that scale. 
  • Needing positional authority to get things done. Engineering, finance, and compliance sit on separate reporting lines, and you will coordinate across all three every day. You need to find ways to unblock yourself.

Algorithm research
